terms.comment: The genre and a single play. To put one on is cōmoediam agere (Ter. Heaut. prol.), to watch one spectāre, to read one legere (Plin. Ep. 6.21.2). Pliny called his villa down by the water Cōmoedia and the one on the heights Tragoedia (Plin. Ep. 9.7.3).

terms.gloss: of comedy, comic; as a noun, a comic poet
evidence: Plaut. Capt. 4.1.11: ut cōmicī servī solent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What belongs to comedy or appears in it: cōmicī senēs, the stock old men of the stage. It is not “funny” in general (see funny).

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Com. 30; Quint. 1.11.1; Plin. Ep. 1.15.2 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: An actor of comedy, as against histriō, any actor.

phrases.latin: cēnantī mihi, sī cum uxōre vel paucīs, liber legitur; post cēnam cōmoedia aut lyristēs
phrases.english: when I dine with my wife or a few friends, a book is read; after dinner, a comedy or a lyre-player

sources: Lewis & Short: comoedia · Lewis & Short: comicus · Lewis & Short: comoedus
Pliny from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-plinius); the other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 52.
